- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast, especially in early/peak of 30d horizon — reduce forecast peaks by 15–30%.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral, model often under-responds — increase forecast lows by 10–20% to avoid underestimating downside.
- Model consistently over-estimates short-term spikes (e.g., 1–3 day peaks) after bullish sentiment — apply smoothing filter to dampen overshoots.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon — if forecast is >2σ above recent 18-day mean, reduce by 20–40%.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust — apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 10–15% for next 3–5 days.
- Forecasting horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence — cap maximum deviation at ±1.5x recent 18-day range unless sentiment strongly supports extreme move.
